name: Sabal Palm
quote: The sabal palmetto palm, which is also known as the cabbage palm, and sometimes as the cabbage palmetto, a tree native to Florida, is hereby designated as the Florida state tree.

name: Moonstone
yaml_legislation: Adopted by the Florida Legislature in 1970
quote: The moonstone, a transparent or translucent feldspar of pearly or opaline luster, is hereby designated the Florida state gem.

name: Agatized Coral
yaml_legislation: Adopted by the Florida Legislature in 1979
quote: Agatized coral, a chalcedony pseudomorph after coral, appearing as limestone geodes lined with botryoidal agate or quartz crystals and drusy quartz fingers, indigenous to Florida, is hereby designated the Florida state stone.

name: Zebra Longwing
quote: The Zebra Longwing (Heliconius charitonius) is designated the official state butterfly.

name: American Alligator
yaml_legislation: Adopted by the Florida Legislature in 1987
quote: The American alligator is hereby designated and declared as the official Florida state reptile.

name: Florida Largemouth Bass
quote: The Florida largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides floridanus) is hereby designated and declared as the official Florida state freshwater fish.

name: Atlantic Sailfish
quote: The Atlantic sailfish (Istiophorus platypterus) is hereby designated and declared as the official Florida state saltwater fish.

name: Orange
yaml_legislation: Adopted by the Florida Legislature in 2005
quote: The orange (Citrus sinensis and hybrids thereof) is hereby designated the official fruit of Florida.

name: Old Folks at Home
yaml_legislation: Adopted by the Florida Legislature in 1935; revised lyrics adopted in 2008
quote: The song “Old Folks at Home,” revised lyrics, as adopted by the Center for American Music, Stephen Foster Memorial, at the University of Pittsburgh, is designated as the official song of the State of Florida.
